newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour denies minimum wage to swell spending.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour denies minimum wage to swell spending.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party on Wednesday denied claims by the ruling Conservatives that its plan to introduce a minimum wage in Britain could push up public spending by 3.7 billion stg a year.
Economics spokesman Gordon Brown said that, in setting the level of the minimum wage, Labour would take the impact on the economy into account as well as its effect on employment.

"The minimum wage is something that will be examined in government and it will be set in line with employment considerations and in line with the economic considerations of the time," Brown told a news conference.
The Conservatives published a document earlier claiming that spending pledges already made by Labour would raise public spending by 30 billion stg.

Of this, it said 3.7 billion would be accounted for by a minimum wage assuming it was set at 50 percent of male average earnings and that there was then a 50 percent recouping of former wage differentials.
The Conservatives said the effect would be caused by increases in wages in the public sector.
But in a document issued to rebut what it called "Tory lies" on its spending plans, Labour claimed that if anything the minimum wage could cut spending.

"Far from costing public money, the minimum wage will end the scandal of unscrupulous employers being subisidised at the expense of the taxpayer, and will rescue the spiralling costs of in-work benefits to the low paid, currently costing 2.4 billion stg," the document said.
